readiness_evidence: First release on PyPI; there is no earlier installed version to be compatible with.

A paid booking passed end to end on 16/10/2026 with the release candidate: Link sign-in, search area, discovery, native checkout, slot selection, buyer from Link, booking, spend approval, and confirmation.
releases.user_summary: First public release of the booking assistant.

readiness_evidence: No request or response exchanged with the registry or with businesses changes: the platform profile, USP and UCP versions, and every booking call are as in 0.1.0.
The saved booking file keeps format 2. The only new field is optional and at the top level, which 0.1.0 ignores, so moving between 0.1.0 and 0.2.0 in either direction keeps every saved booking.
The full test suite passes, including new tests for older and newer saved bookings and for the update consent, decline, and install paths.
releases.user_summary: The booking assistant can now tell you when a newer version is ready and install it when you agree.

readiness_evidence: PyPI serves PEP 740 provenance for both published files: the integrity endpoint returns HTTP 200 for booking_agent_cli-0.3.0-py3-none-any.whl and booking_agent_cli-0.3.0.tar.gz, the publisher is GitHub wix/booking-agent workflow release.yml, and pypi-attestations verify pypi --repository https://github.com/wix/booking-agent prints OK for both. gh attestation verify --repo wix/booking-agent also passes for the wheel.

A clean uv tool install of 0.3.0 from PyPI passes its own first-run check against the live provenance on the first flow init. After one installed file was edited, flow init and flow pay request refused with installation_unverified and a reinstall command; restoring the file cleared it.
No request or response exchanged with the registry or with businesses changes: the platform profile, USP and UCP versions, and every booking call are as in 0.2.0.

Saved bookings move both ways: with one session file, 0.2.0 started a booking, 0.3.0 listed it and added another, 0.2.0 then read the file and added a third while keeping the two new optional fields, and 0.3.0 read all three. The file keeps format 2.
releases.user_summary: The booking assistant now checks that updates and its own installation come from the official release before it books or pays.

readiness_evidence: PyPI serves PEP 740 provenance for both 0.4.0 files: /integrity/booking-agent-cli/0.4.0/<file>/provenance returns HTTP 200 for booking_agent_cli-0.4.0-py3-none-any.whl and booking_agent_cli-0.4.0.tar.gz (checked 18/10/26).

Release v0.4.0 carries SKILL.md and SKILL.md.sigstore.json as assets, and tag skill-v0.50.0 still points at 4f08016f, the commit that released it; the repository's 'release tags' ruleset blocks update, deletion and non-fast-forward on refs/tags/skill-v*, so the pinned skill cannot move.

No installed assistant can land on 0.4.0: select_target() in updates.py picks the newest release that is not deferred or withdrawn, and update --user-confirmed installs that exact version's verified wheel, so with 0.4.1 recommended the target is always 0.4.1. 0.4.0 is recommended only so that it does not block 0.4.1 behind it, since a release after a deferred one is never offered.

Anyone already pinned to 0.4.0 is carried past the raw-byte-hash bug rather than left on it: 0.4.1 is recommended and lists the booking and payment capabilities, so the assistant offers the move before any request that needs them.

No external contract changed: USP and UCP requests and responses, the registry calls, and platform-profile.json are byte-identical to 0.3.0, so existing businesses and the registry in use today are unaffected (git diff v0.3.0..v0.4.1 touches no profile or protocol file).

Saved session files stay safe both ways: the release adds one optional field (skill_integrity_failure) and leaves SCHEMA_VERSION and STORE_SCHEMA_VERSION at 2, so an older build still opens a file this one wrote.
releases.user_summary: The booking assistant now checks that its own instructions are the official ones before it books or pays.

readiness_evidence: PyPI serves PEP 740 provenance for both 0.4.1 files: /integrity/booking-agent-cli/0.4.1/<file>/provenance returns HTTP 200 for booking_agent_cli-0.4.1-py3-none-any.whl and booking_agent_cli-0.4.1.tar.gz (checked 18/10/26).

gh attestation verify --repo wix/booking-agent --signer-workflow wix/booking-agent/.github/workflows/release.yml succeeds (exit 0) on a copy freshly fetched from the pinned raw URL for skill-v0.51.0, with the attestation naming release.yml at 56845d9b; the same command on a modified copy exits 1 with no attestation for its digest.

skill-install-check passes on master (run 39118894450, 18/10/26): npx skills add leaves two installed copies, .agents/skills/booking-agent/SKILL.md byte-identical and agent/skills/booking-agent/SKILL.md rewritten by the installer, and the CLI accepts both; OpenClaw installs the skill unchanged and it is accepted.

A clean uv pip install booking-agent-cli==0.4.1 from PyPI accepts both the attested skill and an installer-rewritten copy (description refolded from | to > and rewrapped, allowed-tools and user-invocable dropped) at flow init --skill-path, and still returns skill_unverified for a tampered copy, which blocks flow pay request.

No external contract changed: USP and UCP requests and responses, the registry calls, and platform-profile.json are byte-identical to 0.3.0, so existing businesses and the registry in use today are unaffected (git diff v0.3.0..v0.4.1 touches no profile or protocol file).

Saved session files stay safe both ways: the release adds one optional field (skill_integrity_failure) and leaves SCHEMA_VERSION and STORE_SCHEMA_VERSION at 2, so an older build still opens a file this one wrote.
